availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

recipes.name: autoresearch
recipes.description: Repeatedly proposes and applies one experiment at a time, runs the benchmark, and keeps changes only when they beat the current best result.

recipes.name: feature-pipeline
recipes.description: Full feature pipeline in the given workdir: requirements, reviewed design loop, plan, implement-and-review loop with two-model review, fail-closed validation gate. Heavy; for hard multi-file tasks.

recipes.name: goal
recipes.description: Iterative agent loop toward a single verifiable goal until self-verified complete or the iteration budget is exhausted; no external progress state, each iteration re-derives progress from the repo.

recipes.name: investigate
recipes.description: Single-step read-only investigation. The orchestrator supplies a self-contained brief; a planner agent investigates and writes a findings report.

recipes.name: publish-pr
recipes.description: Opens a PR from a branch (reuses an existing open PR), then watches and responds to feedback until a terminal state. run_dir: required per-run artifact dir; repo_dir: target repo (optional).

recipes.name: ralph
recipes.description: Loops one coding agent through a JSON checklist file, one item per iteration, until every item is done; progress is durable and inspectable mid-run. For a single non-decomposable outcome, use goal.

recipes.name: semantic-review-multi-model
recipes.description: Reviews a change with two independent semantic reviewers in parallel on different models, then aggregates into one issues-only report under <workdir>/.agents/reviews/. Reviewers never see each other.
